analysis.title: GS Navin - The Red A Breakdown of October 15th in Asia
key_insights: Asia equity markets sold off sharply on 15 Oct 2026. Desk notional traded was up 58% vs the previous 20-day average, and the desk was 1.2x better to sell overall.

The desk was net to sell in every market except Australia (1.4x better to buy). By sector it was most active in Information Technology (1.4x better to sell), Industrials (1.1x better to sell) and Materials (1.1x better to sell). Consumer Discretionary and Consumer Staples were flat.

The desk described no panic in the flow, but selling was robust and ran through the entire session rather than the usual early-morning concentration. Traders who expected a bounce kept returning to the market. Defensive sectors were also sold, to a lesser extent.

Taiwan: TWSE fell 3.4% on the largest foreign institutional investor (FII) net-selling day in history, about USD 9.3bn. The size of the move combined with high turnover was arguably the largest of the past year. Only the -3.6% move on 6/26 saw higher activity.
TSMC earnings after the close were mostly in line. The desk says that is likely not enough to turn sentiment more positive, and KOSPI and Taiwan futures kept falling after the announcement.

Korea: KOSPI fell 7.6%, the largest selloff since July 28, 2026. Circuit breakers triggered for both KOSPI and KOSDAQ for the first time since July 29. Semiconductors closed down 12%, driven by foreign selling of $3.6bn.

SK Hynix: foreigners net sold $830m, extending selling to 15 consecutive sessions. Retail (+$340m) and local institutions (+$50m) bought but did not offset it. Samsung: foreigners net sold $1.1bn, a 5-day streak, while retail (+$670m) and local institutions (+$375m) bought the dip.

Japan: Nikkei fell 4.90%, the worst day since March 9. GS's Japan semiconductor basket (GSXAJSEM) fell 11.6%, its third-largest drawdown since creation. KIOXIA closed below its 200-day moving average for the first time in its history.
Japan desk flows were +85% vs the month-to-date average and 40% above the year-to-date average. The desk saw more nontraditional flow, with no panic.

Hong Kong was relatively stable: HSI fell 1.03%. Every thematic sector closed lower, led by China Optical Network (-5.08%), China Data Centers (-4.76%) and China AI Value (-3.72%). Southbound investors net sold $647m, the largest in over two weeks, and market notional was up 38% vs the previous 3-week average.
